lessons.name: SIM XR
lessons.summary: SIM XR collects human demonstrations in virtual reality to improve robot models on specific tasks, with results measured in simulation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

SIM XR collects human demonstrations in virtual reality to improve robot models on specific tasks, with results measured in simulation.

![SIM XR simulation case-study video still](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-sim-xr.webp)
*SIM XR simulation case-study video still. Source: [SIM XR](https://simxr.tech/what-we-do/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The customer brings a failing job:** SIM XR rebuilds the scene in simulation, a computer-run physical environment, rather than collecting directly on the robot.
- **People demonstrate in VR:** virtual reality headsets let operators guide a simulated robot; the recorded movements become training examples.
- **A policy is the action-producing model:** SIM XR can supply demonstrations alone or further train the customer’s existing policy.

> **Key idea:** A useful demonstration dataset targets a measured failure, not merely a large recording count.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think regression testing:** keep the same evaluation protocol before and after training so a changed score means something.
- **A concrete company-reported example:** 50 VR demonstrations led to 27 successes in 30 paired trials; these were simulation results, not hardware validation.
- **Connect this to LeRobot:** SIM XR offers LeRobot-format exports, making data structure and replay checks useful topics for a software-focused lab.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the short case:** separate scene reconstruction, demonstration collection, and evaluation in your notes.
2. **Sketch a student experiment:** define one pick-and-place task and a pass/fail rule before gathering examples.
3. **Use the public sprint inquiry:** ask about observation fields, action units, and a hardware-transfer test; do not equate simulation success with deployment.

lessons.name: Sitegeist
lessons.summary: Sitegeist builds modular construction robots for tasks such as concrete removal, sandblasting, and drilling.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Sitegeist builds modular construction robots for tasks such as concrete removal, sandblasting, and drilling.

![Sitegeist construction robot](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-sitegeist.webp)
*Sitegeist construction robot. Source: [Sitegeist](https://sitegeist-robotics.com/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **One platform, different jobs:** Sitegeist presents a modular construction robot rather than a general household assistant.
- **Hydrodemolition means water-based demolition:** it is one of the company’s applications, alongside sandblasting and drilling.
- **The task is physical:** reaching corners, columns, and ceilings matters as well as moving a tool across a broad surface.

> **Key idea:** A robot’s useful capability depends on its tool and worksite, not just its AI model.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think plugin architecture:** the platform is the host; a task-specific tool changes what work the machine can perform.
- **A concrete comparison:** drilling needs hole position and depth; sandblasting needs surface coverage. Use those different outputs when designing an evaluation.
- **Software meets construction:** Sitegeist is a useful counterpoint to tabletop manipulation because the work happens on existing structures, not neatly arranged objects.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the founder interview:** the German-language DIGITALWERK episode introduces the company and construction setting.
2. **Study the official applications:** choose one operation and list its inputs, desired result, and likely stopping conditions on paper.
3. **Use the public contact page:** propose a focused technical talk about adapting robots to construction tasks, not an assumed hardware loan.

lessons.name: Skild AI
lessons.summary: Skild AI develops Skild Brain, a robot-control model intended to transfer skills across different robot bodies and tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Skild AI develops Skild Brain, a robot-control model intended to transfer skills across different robot bodies and tasks.

![Robotic manipulation in Skild AI’s demonstration](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-skild-ai.webp)
*Robotic manipulation in Skild AI’s demonstration. Source: [Skild AI](https://www.skild.ai/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The product is a brain, not one robot:** Skild Brain targets arms, mobile manipulators, quadrupeds, and humanoids.
- **Omni-bodied is the company’s term:** it means aiming for one controller across many physical bodies, not a separate hand-written program per machine.
- **Training combines sources:** Skild describes simulation and human videos, followed by robot demonstrations and operational data.

> **Key idea:** Sharing a model across robots is a generalization problem, not proof that every new robot will work.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a portable runtime:** the same program idea must survive different hardware capabilities; a wheeled base cannot execute a human hand movement literally.
- **A worked example from the company:** jammed wheels make a wheeled quadruped switch to walking; compare that demonstrated recovery with its broader marketing claims.
- **Connect to Skild Brain:** distinguish a successful edited demonstration from measured performance across tasks, starting conditions, and robot bodies.

## How to engage

1. **Start with the official video:** identify what the human demonstrates and what the robot actually executes.
2. **Read the body-transfer article:** note which robots were excluded from training and how failures are presented.
3. **Use public company channels:** ask a precise evaluation question; do not plan a student project around unconfirmed access to model weights.

lessons.name: SquareMind
lessons.summary: SquareMind develops Swan, a robotic imaging system that captures detailed skin images to support dermatologists and follow changes between visits.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

SquareMind develops Swan, a robotic imaging system that captures detailed skin images to support dermatologists and follow changes between visits.

![SquareMind Swan robotic skin-imaging system](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-squaremind.webp)
*SquareMind Swan robotic skin-imaging system. Source: [SquareMind](https://www.squaremind.com/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Swan automates image capture:** the system moves a camera around the body to collect detailed skin views.
- **Dermoscopy means close-up skin examination:** Swan aims to extend that detail to full-body imaging rather than isolated photographs.
- **Software connects the visits:** the EU project report describes robotic planning, image processing, secure storage, and AI for detecting new or modified moles.

> **Key idea:** Repeatable image acquisition is a robotics contribution even when the final decision belongs to a clinician.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think versioned snapshots:** useful comparisons require matching the same region across visits, not merely saving two unrelated image folders.
- **A concrete example:** the project report describes flagging a new or changed mole between visits; detecting change is different from declaring cancer.
- **Connect to Swan:** this is a perception-and-motion product, showing why robotics includes careful sensing rather than only grasping or walking.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official introduction:** notice the robot’s position relative to the person and the areas it images.
2. **Read the EU reporting page:** separate reported engineering work from the project’s hoped-for clinical impact.
3. **Contact the public company address:** propose a talk on repeatable imaging; use non-medical objects for a student camera-positioning exercise, not diagnostic experiments.

lessons.name: Stanley Robotics
lessons.summary: Stanley Robotics builds robots and fleet software that lift and move ordinary cars for parking and outdoor vehicle logistics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Stanley Robotics builds robots and fleet software that lift and move ordinary cars for parking and outdoor vehicle logistics.

![Stanley Robotics vehicle-moving robot](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-stanley-robotics.webp)
*Stanley Robotics vehicle-moving robot. Source: [Stanley Robotics](https://www.stanley-robotics.com/meet-our-robots/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Stan moves the car for you:** the robot finds a vehicle, lifts it, carries it, and parks it in an assigned space.
- **Fleet management allocates work:** central software chooses jobs and routes; individual robots sense obstacles while moving.
- **The service includes software:** stock management tracks cars, while connections to flight information or delivery planning help decide when vehicles are needed.

> **Key idea:** Automating a car park does not require making every parked car self-driving.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a job queue with mobile workers:** dispatch decisions belong to the fleet, but each robot must execute its own movement safely.
- **A concrete example:** an airport flight update changes when a car is needed; the software can adjust vehicle flows rather than follow a fixed parking order.
- **Study system boundaries:** Stanley Robotics illustrates how route planning, physical lifting, and customer-system integration become one useful service.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official Stan animation:** follow the pickup and placement sequence before reading the software description.
2. **Prototype only the scheduler:** represent cars and spaces as records and test how a changed pickup time alters your proposed queue.
3. **Use the public contact page:** ask about fleet coordination or a technical presentation; keep students away from experiments involving lifted vehicles.

lessons.name: Starkenn SilMach Labs (SilMach)
lessons.summary: Starkenn SilMach Labs develops silicon micromotors, mechanical event sensors, and custom miniature mechanisms rather than complete general-purpose robots.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Starkenn SilMach Labs develops silicon micromotors, mechanical event sensors, and custom miniature mechanisms rather than complete general-purpose robots.

![Opened SilMach silicon micromotor](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-starkenn-silmach-labs-silmach.webp)
*Opened SilMach silicon micromotor. Source: [Starkenn SilMach Labs (SilMach)](https://www.silmach.com/en/powermems), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **MEMS means microelectromechanical systems:** tiny mechanical structures are made with techniques related to silicon electronics.
- **PowerMEMS produces motion:** these programmable micromotors use electrostatic actuation, meaning electrical attraction creates movement, rather than conventional magnetic motor operation.
- **ChronoMEMS records events mechanically:** its sensors detect or count threshold crossings, such as shocks, without an electrical power supply for sensing.

> **Key idea:** A robotics supplier may provide a tiny motion or sensing component, not a finished robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think event logging in hardware:** a mechanical counter can retain evidence of an excessive load without continuously streaming measurements to a computer.
- **A numerical example:** PowerMEMS lists 360 steps per revolution; one full turn divided by 360 gives one degree per commanded step.
- **Keep scale in view:** the listed micromotors were designed primarily for watches; that does not establish that they can drive a student robot arm.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the watch-movement video:** it makes silicon micromotors tangible, despite not being a robotics deployment.
2. **Compare the two product families:** write down which creates motion and which stores evidence of an event.
3. **Use the official contact form:** describe a specific miniature mechanism and its load before asking about feasibility; deployed robotics customers remain unknown here.

lessons.name: Starship Technologies
lessons.summary: Starship Technologies operates small sidewalk robots that deliver groceries, food, and other goods, with remote human assistance available when needed.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Starship Technologies operates small sidewalk robots that deliver groceries, food, and other goods, with remote human assistance available when needed.

![Starship delivery robot rolling through a park](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-starship-technologies.webp)
*Starship delivery robot rolling through a park. Source: [Starship Technologies](https://www.starship.xyz/our-robots/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The robot is a wheeled cargo box:** six wheels carry a locked compartment along sidewalks rather than a passenger along roads.
- **Sensors support local navigation:** Starship lists cameras, radar, and ultrasonic sensors, which use sound echoes to detect nearby objects.
- **People remain available:** remote assistants can help when needed, while critical safety functions run on the robot even if its internet connection drops.

> **Key idea:** A delivery service needs both autonomous movement and a reliable handoff to the customer.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a distributed service:** the app requests delivery, the robot handles movement, and the phone authorizes opening the compartment.
- **A concrete delivery:** groceries are loaded into the insulated compartment; the robot travels to the customer, who unlocks it using their phone.
- **Connect to Starship delivery robot:** distinguish planning a route from handling pedestrians, road crossings, connectivity loss, and an unavailable recipient.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a day in operation:** note the loading, travel, and customer handoff rather than only the robot’s appearance.
2. **Read the autonomy FAQ:** explain in your own words where remote assistance fits without calling every trip remote-controlled.
3. **Use public business channels for questions:** propose a student talk on sidewalk navigation; test a miniature delivery workflow indoors, away from public traffic.

lessons.name: Synapticon
lessons.summary: Synapticon supplies servo drives, integrated motion hardware, and control tools that turn robot movement commands into controlled motor motion.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Synapticon supplies servo drives, integrated motion hardware, and control tools that turn robot movement commands into controlled motor motion.

![Synapticon SOMANET Circulo circular servo drive](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-synapticon.webp)
*Synapticon SOMANET Circulo circular servo drive. Source: [Synapticon](https://www.synapticon.com/produkte/somanet-circulo), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A servo drive controls a motor:** it adjusts electrical output using measured feedback rather than simply switching power on.
- **SOMANET Circulo integrates joint electronics:** the circular board combines drive functions with options for position sensing and brake control.
- **An encoder measures position:** Circulo can use feedback from both the motor and the gearbox output, where mechanical transmission changes the motion.

> **Key idea:** A robot brain chooses actions; dependable joint electronics make those actions physically controllable.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a hardware device driver with feedback:** a requested movement must become measured motor behavior, not merely a successfully sent command.
- **A numerical example:** the product page lists encoders up to 20-bit resolution; that represents 1,048,576 possible codes, not guaranteed mechanical accuracy.
- **Separate component from system:** Synapticon-Stabilus humanoid actuators is a related map node, but a drive alone is not a complete joint or humanoid.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Circulo introduction:** locate the drive, sensor, and brake functions before comparing specifications.
2. **Read the product documentation entry:** trace a command, feedback measurement, and stop condition on paper before touching powered hardware.
3. **Use public support or demo channels:** ask about one specific motor-and-encoder combination; do not assume compatibility from a board’s shape alone.

lessons.name: Telexistence
lessons.summary: Telexistence develops AI-driven and remotely operated robots, including TX Ghost systems that restock drinks in convenience stores.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Telexistence develops AI-driven and remotely operated robots, including TX Ghost systems that restock drinks in convenience stores.

![Telexistence beverage-restocking robot](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-telexistence.webp)
*Telexistence beverage-restocking robot. Source: [Telexistence](https://tx-inc.com/en/home/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **TX Ghost handles drinks:** the September 2025 announcement describes pilots at selected Tokyo 7-Eleven stores, not every branch.
- **Autonomy and teleoperation coexist:** autonomy means robot-directed operation; teleoperation means a person controls the robot remotely when needed.
- **Learning targets difficult exceptions:** Telexistence and Physical Intelligence describe using operational data to improve recovery from errors in drink restocking.

> **Key idea:** Human intervention can be both an operational fallback and a source of examples for improving autonomy.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think exception handling:** normal shelf stocking is the main path; an awkward bottle creates a recovery branch that still needs a solution.
- **A real example from the partnership announcement:** recovering a rolled-over beverage inside a display shelf was difficult to automate with existing technology.
- **Connect to TX Ghost:** evaluate the whole workflow, including recovery, rather than counting only successful grasps in a clean demonstration.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official stocking video:** identify where drinks start, how the robot reaches them, and where they end up.
2. **Read both 2025 announcements:** separate pilot deployment evidence from the partnership’s future goal of automating more error recovery.
3. **Use public company inquiries:** propose a talk on learning from interventions; prototype a tabletop recovery task instead of assuming access to store data.

lessons.name: Tethys Robotics
lessons.summary: Tethys Robotics builds underwater inspection robots that help operators map structures and hold position in murky, moving water.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Tethys Robotics builds underwater inspection robots that help operators map structures and hold position in murky, moving water.

![Tethys One underwater inspection robot](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-tethys-robotics.webp)
*Tethys One underwater inspection robot. Source: [Tethys Robotics](https://www.tethys-robotics.ch/product), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Tethys One is the platform:** a compact underwater vehicle carries cameras, navigation sensors, and optional inspection tools rather than swimming like a person.
- **Sonar uses sound echoes:** it helps operators inspect structures when suspended particles make ordinary camera images difficult to interpret.
- **Position holding counters water movement:** the product supports staying near a structure while an operator examines it or records inspection data.

> **Key idea:** Underwater inspection needs a trustworthy estimate of position even when the camera cannot see clearly.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think observability for infrastructure:** the robot collects evidence about physical assets, much as monitoring software collects evidence about a running service.
- **A concrete example:** mark a damaged area as a point of interest during an inspection, then include its location in the recorded report.
- **Study sensor roles:** compare the camera view, sound-based measurements, and resulting map; each answers a different question about the same structure.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official introduction:** identify the vehicle, operator equipment, and underwater inspection setting before reading specifications.
2. **Trace one inspection record:** sketch the information needed to revisit a marked defect rather than merely save an attractive underwater video.
3. **Use the public contact page:** propose a student talk on navigation in poor visibility; a student software interface or hardware loan is unknown.

lessons.name: Theker
lessons.summary: Theker develops adaptable industrial robots whose hardware and intelligence are intended to handle changing factory and warehouse tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Theker develops adaptable industrial robots whose hardware and intelligence are intended to handle changing factory and warehouse tasks.

![Theker official logo](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-theker.webp)
*Theker official logo. Source: [Theker](https://www.theker.ai/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Reconfigurable means physically changeable:** TechCrunch describes robots whose hands, arms, and overall form can be changed for different industrial tasks.
- **Generalist describes an ambition:** Theker targets varied work rather than a machine dedicated permanently to one repeated operation.
- **Adaptation is the product pitch:** its investor describes handling mixed products and irregular shapes without manual reprogramming; these are company-backed claims, not student-reproduced results.

> **Key idea:** A generalist industrial robot does not have to look human; its body can be chosen for the work.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think configurable software:** a reusable engine can serve different applications, but changing the interface still requires checking what the whole system can actually handle.
- **A concrete example:** sorting packages and packing clothing may need different hands; changing a prompt alone does not establish suitable physical handling.
- **Compare map approaches:** Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) covers models connecting images and instructions to actions; Theker illustrates the additional problem of choosing useful hardware.

## How to engage

1. **Start with the founder discussion:** the Itnig conversation is in Spanish; use the Theker segment to hear the industrial framing directly.
2. **Compare reporting with investor claims:** list demonstrated tasks separately from promises about adaptability and deployment.
3. **Write through the official contact:** propose a technical discussion about task changes; public code, student access, and robot prices are unknown here.

lessons.name: Tinamu
lessons.summary: Tinamu combines drones, sensing, and cloud processing to turn industrial inventory scans into measurements and reports.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Tinamu combines drones, sensing, and cloud processing to turn industrial inventory scans into measurements and reports.

![Tinamu drone scanning an industrial space](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-tinamu.webp)
*Tinamu drone scanning an industrial space. Source: [Tinamu](https://tinamu-labs.com/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Inventory means material on site:** Tinamu measures stored bulk materials and tracks changes, rather than delivering parcels or photographing landscapes.
- **Indoor navigation uses computer vision:** software interprets visible features so the automated drone system can navigate without GPS satellite positioning.
- **Two offerings differ:** TINAMU RMS Automated Robotic Monitoring System automates indoor monitoring; RMS light is a separate laser-scanning kit used on drones or handheld.

> **Key idea:** The useful output is a repeatable inventory measurement, not simply a successful drone flight.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a data pipeline:** capture measurements, process them, then deliver structured results to a dashboard or another business system.
- **A concrete example:** measure a stockpile's volume, then combine it with the material's effective density to estimate weight; volume alone is not mass.
- **LiDAR measures with laser light:** its spatial measurements support a digital twin, meaning a computer representation of the physical storage area.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the KIBAG demonstration:** identify what gets scanned and what information the customer needs afterward.
2. **Read the RMS light manual:** distinguish recording a dataset from automated piloting; mounting a sensor does not itself make a drone autonomous.
3. **Use the official enquiry form:** propose an inventory-analysis seminar and ask about sample data; free student datasets and software access are unknown.

lessons.name: Tommoro Robotics
lessons.summary: Tommoro Robotics develops robot intelligence and operational software, linking language-guided learning research with systems for deploying and managing robots.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Tommoro Robotics develops robot intelligence and operational software, linking language-guided learning research with systems for deploying and managing robots.

![Robot hardware shown by Tommoro Robotics](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-tommoro-robotics.webp)
*Robot hardware shown by Tommoro Robotics. Source: [Tommoro Robotics](https://tommoro.ai/en), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Research roots are at Seoul National University:** the company describes developing robot models alongside the software needed to run them outside research experiments.
- **HABILIS Brain 0 supplies learned intelligence:** HABILIS Console addresses data, training, and deployment; these are different responsibilities within the company's stack.
- **CLIP-RT is an accessible research entry:** its public project demonstrates learning robot behavior with language supervision and provides code and pretrained checkpoints.

> **Key idea:** Training a model and operating a reliable robot service are separate engineering problems that must eventually connect.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think an API dispatcher:** CLIP-RT chooses a language-described motion, then a lookup table translates that choice into lower-level robot commands.
- **A concrete example:** the repository uses a camera image and “close the laptop” instruction to select an action from a predefined motion list.
- **Define the vocabulary:** a policy chooses actions from observations; a vision-language-action model combines visual input, language, and robot action selection.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the project-page demonstrations:** compare the task instruction with the smaller movements required to finish it.
2. **Read the repository usage example:** trace image preprocessing, action scoring, and lookup-table translation before considering a hardware experiment.
3. **Send a reproducible research question:** use repository issues or the company's public partnership address; HABILIS student access and pricing are unknown.

lessons.name: TWIICE
lessons.summary: TWIICE develops wearable robotic exoskeletons to help people with spinal cord injuries stand and walk.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TWIICE develops wearable robotic exoskeletons to help people with spinal cord injuries stand and walk.

![TWIICE group photograph with awards](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-twiice.webp)
*TWIICE group photograph with awards. Source: [TWIICE](https://twiice.com/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **An exoskeleton is worn:** its external mechanical structure assists the user's movement instead of transporting them inside a separate vehicle.
- **TWIICE personal exoskeleton is the map platform:** the company focuses on mobility for people with spinal cord injuries, not general warehouse lifting.
- **Design begins with users:** the team describes working alongside patients and caregivers and combining mechanics, embedded software, and human factors.

> **Key idea:** For a wearable robot, ease of putting it on and controlling it is part of the engineering problem, not decoration.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think accessible interface design:** an algorithm can work internally yet fail its purpose if the intended user cannot operate the complete system comfortably.
- **A concrete example:** compare the actions needed to put the device on, stand, and begin walking; treat each transition as an interface requirement.
- **Separate demonstrations from evidence:** the Swiss pilot-study page points toward clinical evaluation; a walking video alone cannot establish suitability for every person.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official homepage video:** observe how the person and wearable device move together rather than focusing only on the mechanism.
2. **Read the mission and team pages:** list usability questions alongside control-software questions for a beginner discussion.
3. **Use the public partner contact:** propose a talk on assistive-robotics design, not patient trials or unsupervised student use.

> **Watch out:** A wearable walking robot directly supports a person; do not turn this reading exercise into an unsupervised walking test.

lessons.name: TwinswHeel
lessons.summary: TwinswHeel builds wheeled logistics robots that carry goods while following people or navigating planned routes.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TwinswHeel builds wheeled logistics robots that carry goods while following people or navigating planned routes.

![TwinswHeel ciTHy logistics robot family](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-twinswheel.webp)
*TwinswHeel ciTHy logistics robot family. Source: [TwinswHeel](https://www.twinswheel.fr/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The ciTHy S assists with carrying:** the small mobile robot can follow a person with goods rather than requiring that person to push a trolley.
- **Follow-me and autonomy differ:** following tracks a paired person; autonomous operation uses a mapped area and planned virtual routes.
- **Remote supervision adds intervention:** the company describes a safety driver who observes the environment and can take control or stop the robot.

> **Key idea:** A delivery robot is a transport service with operating modes and human responsibility, not just navigation software on wheels.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think a state machine:** following, autonomous travel, and remote driving have different inputs and rules for switching control.
- **A concrete example:** if an obstacle blocks a virtual route, the system may go around within allowed bounds or require operator intervention.
- **Study the complete handoff:** sensing an obstacle is different from deciding who may authorize the next movement; both belong in a useful demonstration.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the France24 introduction:** it is an early demonstration, useful for understanding the idea rather than checking today's product capabilities.
2. **Read the operating-mode explanation:** sketch control ownership for each mode and what happens when communication disappears.
3. **Contact the company publicly:** suggest a student talk on supervised urban logistics, using a simulated route example rather than a public-street experiment.

> **Watch out:** Follow-me still requires an attentive responsible operator; it does not make movement around pedestrians automatically safe.

lessons.name: UMA (Universal Mechanical Assistant)
lessons.summary: UMA (Universal Mechanical Assistant) is a Paris robotics startup developing general-purpose robots, including its Northstar humanoid design and Version 0 prototype.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

UMA (Universal Mechanical Assistant) is a Paris robotics startup developing general-purpose robots, including its Northstar humanoid design and Version 0 prototype.

![UMA robot design published on its official website](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-uma-universal-mechanical-assistant.webp)
*UMA robot design published on its official website. Source: [UMA (Universal Mechanical Assistant)](https://uma.bot/), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Northstar is a robot design:** UMA describes a body for navigating different environments and hands intended to use tools.
- **Version 0 is the first prototype:** the company distinguishes this hardware-and-software integration milestone from the Northstar design in its launch post.
- **Industrial work is an intended application:** reporting describes manufacturing and logistics ambitions; plans are not evidence of widespread customer deployment.

> **Key idea:** Keep a future robot design, a working prototype, and a deployed product in separate mental boxes.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think prototype versus production service:** an integrated demo proves components can cooperate, but does not establish reliability across every customer's workflow.
- **A concrete example:** build an evidence table with separate columns for Northstar's intended tool use and what Version 0 is actually shown doing.
- **Connect to LeRobot:** co-founder Rémi Cadène previously led that open-source project; this background does not make UMA hardware or its software automatically open source.
- **Read the map carefully:** UMA Northstar humanoid names the platform ambition, not a student kit with established public purchasing instructions.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official Machina keynote:** note which statements describe demonstrations and which describe the next generation of robots.
2. **Compare the launch post with reporting:** distinguish the company's own wording from journalists' interpretation of its plans.
3. **Use public company channels:** propose a focused robot-learning discussion with a reproducible student demo; student hardware access and published robot prices are unknown.

lessons.name: Unchained Robotics
lessons.summary: Unchained Robotics combines a robot-component marketplace with modular automation systems that help manufacturers put robots to work.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Unchained Robotics combines a robot-component marketplace with modular automation systems that help manufacturers put robots to work.

![Unchained Robotics industrial automation equipment](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_5-unchained-robotics.webp)
*Unchained Robotics industrial automation equipment. Source: [Unchained Robotics](https://unchainedrobotics.de/en), unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The marketplace spans brands:** customers compare robots, grippers, cameras, and other components rather than buying only one manufacturer's robot arm.
- **Integration makes components useful:** the company helps select compatible parts and supports moving from an automation idea to an installed system.
- **MalocherBot packages a complete task:** its modular systems include palletizing, meaning stacking boxes or other loads onto a transport pallet.
- **LUNA is the operating software:** it lets users adjust workflows and packaging parameters through an interface rather than writing robot code for every change.

> **Key idea:** Much robotics value comes from making existing hardware work together reliably, not inventing a new arm.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think dependency management:** selecting a robot, gripper, and camera resembles choosing compatible software packages; an attractive component alone does not guarantee a working application.
- **A concrete example:** changing carton dimensions changes a pallet pattern; MalocherBot exposes these settings through its interface instead of requiring a fresh robot program.
- **Study system boundaries:** ask what the supplied cell includes and what the customer still needs to provide, such as product flow and site integration.

## How to engage

1. **Watch an official application video:** identify the arm, gripping tool, incoming goods, and completed physical task.
2. **Compare the marketplace and MalocherBot pages:** distinguish individual components from a packaged automation solution.
3. **Use the public contact channel:** propose a student integration discussion using a paper requirements sheet; a complete industrial cell is not assumed affordable for 42AI.
